headline: Growth holds, margin dips, income normalizes after one-off
summary_short: Q2 revenue rose 13% y/y to $12.56B on membership growth, price increases, and ad revenue, while operating margin slipped to 33.4% as tech and marketing spend outgrew sales. Net income fell to $3.40B, down 36% q/q only because Q1 booked a one-time $2.8B WBD termination fee that Q2 didn't repeat.
summary_long: Revenue grew 13% y/y to $12.56B on membership growth, price increases, and higher ad revenue, with FX providing a modest tailwind; cost of revenue grew in lockstep (+13% y/y) on higher content amortization, leaving gross margin flat near 51.9%. Operating margin slipped ~0.7pt y/y to 33.4% as tech-and-development and sales-and-marketing spend outgrew revenue. Net income of $3.40B and diluted EPS of $0.80 look sharply lower q/q only because Q1 2026 included a one-time $2.8B WBD-transaction termination fee; y/y net income is up. Operating cash flow fell to $1.74B and free cash flow to $1.53B for the same reason. Cash fell to $9.10B, mostly from $4.7B of quarterly buybacks; total debt was roughly flat.

drivers.explanation: Growth driven by membership growth, price increases, and higher advertising revenue; FX was a modest y/y tailwind.
Increase was primarily due to higher content amortization on existing and new titles — "a $479 million increase in content amortization."
Revenue and cost of revenue grew at nearly the same y/y rate (+13.4% each), leaving gross margin effectively unchanged.
Technology-and-development and sales-and-marketing expenses grew "at a faster rate than revenue," per the filing.
Q1 FY2026 included a "$2.8 billion termination fee" from the WBD deal's termination; Q2 had no equivalent item, so the q/q drop overstates the underlying trend — y/y net income rose.
Mirrors the net income swing — Q1's one-off WBD fee, not a Q2 earnings decline, drives the sequential drop in diluted EPS.
Sequential drop mainly reflects the absence of Q1's one-off WBD fee inflow plus higher content-asset payments in Q2.
Cash declined mainly from $4.7 billion of share repurchases executed in the quarter.
Net debt rose mainly because cash fell (from buybacks); gross debt was nearly flat q/q.
